blocks.x: SMITHSONIAN INSTITUTION

Interview with Lawrence Brown
by Patricia Willard
Reel Four

Los Angeles, California
July 1976

PRO-TYPISTS, INC.
PROFESSIONAL TRANSCRIPTION SERVICE
AREA CODE 202 347-5395
PROCEEDINGS

This is June 19th, 1976, and this is Reel Four of the interview with Lawrence Brown. Lawrence, I noticed in a couple of books references to the alto saxophone at least -- that you played the alto saxophone very briefly, and when you were very young. How long did you play the alto? How old were you?

Oh, I don't exactly remember how old, but I guess at that time I was more or less just jumping around, trying to find some sort of an instrument that I would like. And it was an attractive horn in that they made them -- finished them with all kinds of colors in those days. And that probably attracted me first of all. And then I wanted to get a better acquaintance with reed instruments. I didn't know. There was a possibility that I might like reed instruments. So, I picked it up and tried it for a while.
You said that saxophones were made in different colors.
Yes, red, green, blue, any color you wanted, similar to the way they finish off pots and pans now with that porcelain stuff.
But the basic instrument was brass?
Oh, yes. Yes. The base -- of this -- all of this was just a covering over the basic brass instrument.
Do you remember what color saxophone attracted you?
No, I had no special color. I was just interested in the tone. In fact, at first the -- C- melody was the popular instrument. I don't think alto had gained too much recognition in those days.
But it was the alto that you played, right?
No, I forget which one. I think it was the C-melody. Because I don't remember when the alto first came into prominence.
When you played the saxophone, was this after you played the tuba and before you played the violin, and where in the progression?
It was after the tuba all right, but I don't remember exactly. I was fumbling around with almost any instrument to try to get the sound in my head and find out whether I even liked it or not.
About how long did you play the saxophone?
Oh, I think I put that down in about a couple of months. It had too many keys on it, and besides that reed had a peculiar feeling, and I didn't care too much for that.
Back to the brass mouthpiece.
Yes, I prefered them a little better.
